messages.text:
"You are a game developer making a Mega Man X sprite animation program that works on a PHONE first. I'm attaching a sprite sheet (556x1647 px PNG, solid green background RGB(0,106,0), sprites made by the_wanderer; the character X belongs to Capcom).

GOAL: Write a complete, working program (one HTML file with JavaScript canvas) that plays every animation from the sheet with no errors. Test the logic before giving it to me and fix every bug you find.

MOBILE REQUIREMENTS (most important)
- It must work on a phone in portrait and landscape, with touch only and no keyboard.
- The game canvas scales to the screen width and keeps pixel art sharp (image-rendering: pixelated, no blur).
- On-screen touch controls:
  - Left side: D-pad with Left, Right, Up, Down.
  - Right side: four big round buttons: Jump, Dash, Saber, Buster.
  - Buttons are at least 56px, with space between them so thumbs don't hit two at once.
- Use pointer events and support multi-touch, so I can hold Right and tap Jump at the same time.
- Holding the Buster button charges the shot, and releasing it fires.
- Stop page scrolling, pull-to-refresh, double-tap zoom and text selection (touch-action: none, user-select: none).
- Keep the keyboard controls too for desktop: Arrows/WASD move, Space jump, Z dash, X saber, C buster, T saber ready pose.
- Keep the frame rate smooth (60 ticks per second, fixed timestep).

STEP 1 - SLICE THE SHEET
- Make the green background transparent (exact color 0,106,0).
- Cut each sprite out as its own frame. Sprites sit in horizontal rows. Rows (y ranges in the sheet):
  Stand/idle 42-83 | Buster shoot stand 98-138 | Saber ready pose 144-193
  Slash 1: 200-243 | Slash 2: 252-299 | Slash 3: 309-370 | Dash slash: 382-421
  Run: 432-469 | Run + shoot: 483-520
  Jump: 533-583 | Jump + shoot: 590-639
  Air slash: 652-701 | Rising slash: 710-775 | Fall after rising slash: 788-851 | Plunge: 866-915
  Dash: 929-968 | Dash + shoot: 978-1017
  Ladder climb: 1023-1085 | Ladder slash: 1090-1142
  Effects: shots/hits 1159-1209, charge rings 1422-1479, hit bursts 1487-1523, bullets 1531-1557
- Ignore the credit text box at the very bottom.
- Give every frame a foot anchor (bottom of the boots) so X does not jitter or slide between frames. Slash swooshes make some frames much wider than the body, so anchor on the boots, not the frame edges.
- The sprites face right. Mirror them for facing left.

STEP 2 - ANIMATIONS (each row above is one animation)
Idle (looping), run (short start frame, then loop), jump (takeoff, rise, hang, fall, land), dash (start, loop, skid stop), 3-hit saber combo on a ground tap, dash slash, air slash, rising slash (Up + Saber), plunge (Down + Saber in the air), buster shoot variants for idle/run/jump/dash, ladder climb and ladder slash, saber ready pose, charge shot with rings.
Use about 3-6 ticks per frame at 60 ticks per second.

STEP 3 - NO MISTAKES CHECK
Before replying, verify: every frame loads, no animation points at a missing frame, X never leaves the screen or floor, every state returns to idle, a combo can chain 3 hits, and two touch buttons can be held at once. Add an \"Animations\" screen that lists every animation, with big tap targets, so I can preview each one frame by frame on my phone.

Give me the full code in one block, then list anything that did not work.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, phone-first Mega Man X sprite animation program as one HTML file with JavaScript canvas, and verify it works.

## Requirements
- Portrait/landscape touch play, crisp canvas scaling, multi-touch controls, 60 Hz fixed timestep, no scrolling/zoom/selection; retain desktop keyboard controls.
- Slice the specified sprite-sheet rows, remove exact green background RGB(0,106,0), anchor frames at the boots, mirror sprites, and implement all requested animations and effects.
- Include an Animations screen for frame-by-frame preview; verify frames, animation references, bounds, combo chaining, and simultaneous touch inputs.
- User asked for the complete code in one block and a list of anything that did not work.

## Decisions
- No sprite sheet was present in the repository, so the page provides a procedurally drawn pixel-art fallback until a user loads the sheet with the LOAD SHEET control.
- Sprite-sheet slicing detects contiguous horizontal pixel runs within the specified y ranges; frame foot anchors are derived from opaque pixels near the bottom of each crop.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with canvas game, touch/keyboard controls, sprite-sheet loader/slicer, animation list/preview, fallback sprites, and runtime validation.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully.
- Headless Chromium tests verified mobile action buttons are 78×78, all 20 animation options are listed, test-sheet loading produces frames without page errors, and the preview works.
- Latest screenshot was saved and inspected at `/tmp/opencode/game-check.jpg`.

### Active
- Review/fix gameplay edge cases and accurately communicate limitations, including whether every requested animation/state and verification check is genuinely satisfied.
- Decide whether to provide the full HTML code in the final response or refer the user to the created file.

### Blocked
- The original sprite sheet was not attached/available, so appearance and slicing against the actual artwork remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` and improve any gameplay or animation-state defects found.
2. Run additional browser checks for touch pointer concurrency, buster charge/release, combo chaining, and floor/screen bounds.
3. Respond with the requested code and disclose that actual sprite-sheet visuals were not tested because the sheet was unavailable; note any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Test command `node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('index.html','utf8').match(/<script>([\\s\\S]*?)<\\/script>/)[1];new Function(s);console.log('JavaScript syntax OK')"` passed.
- A generated synthetic sheet test loaded 92 frames with no browser errors; this does not establish compatibility with the actual attachment.
- Initial page load showed a 404 for an unrelated resource; later synthetic-sheet run filtered that expected 404 and recorded no other errors.
- The implemented game currently uses generic fallback art, and a few moves/animation sequencing details may not fully match the user’s requested semantics.
